13-Week Cash Flow Forecast for Small Business

See every week's cash position for the next quarter, spot the tight weeks before they happen, and track forecast against actual.
Monthly profit-and-loss reports hide timing. A month can be profitable on paper while payroll lands two days before the biggest customer pays. A weekly view shows that gap in advance, while there is still time to move a payment, chase an invoice or arrange a credit line.
What's included
- Weekly view of the next 13 weeks: receipts, payments by category, net cash flow and closing balance
- Automatic BELOW BUFFER flag for any week under the minimum balance you set
- Summary: quarter totals, ending cash, lowest balance, number of tight weeks
- Variance sheet to compare your real bank balance with the forecast each week
- Formulas locked against accidental overwrites; inputs clearly marked in yellow
- PDF guide with a worked example and a field-by-field reference
Who it's for
- Owners of small and service businesses who pay staff weekly or bi-weekly
- Freelancers and agencies with lumpy client payments
- Bookkeepers preparing a cash view for a client or a bank
- Anyone asked by a lender for a short-term cash forecast
You get: 13_week_cash_flow_forecast.xlsx (Inputs, Forecast, Summary, Variance) and this guide.

Rental Property Deal Analyzer

Compare up to 25 buy-and-hold rental deals side by side: monthly cash flow, cap rate, cash-on-cash return, DSCR and a clear verdict against your own targets.
This analyzer puts every deal through the same full calculation: financing, operating costs, reserves for vacancy, maintenance and capital expenses, then net operating income, monthly cash flow and the standard return measures lenders and investors use, so you can compare deals on the same terms.
What's included
- One row per property, up to 25 deals compared side by side
- Mortgage payment (PMT), NOI, monthly cash flow, cap rate, cash-on-cash return, DSCR and rent-to-price
- Vacancy, maintenance, management and CapEx reserves built in, so the numbers are not best-case
- Verdict per deal against the cash-on-cash and DSCR targets you set
- Handles cash purchases (100% down) as well as financed deals
- PDF guide with three worked example deals and a field-by-field reference
Who it's for
- First-time and small portfolio rental investors
- House hackers comparing a duplex against a single-family home
- Agents and wholesalers presenting numbers to buyers

- Effective hourly rate for every fixed-fee project

fields.text:
Freelance Project Profitability & Effective Hourly Rate Tracker

Log each fixed-fee project's fee, estimated and actual hours and direct costs, and see the hourly rate you really earned, hour overruns, and how far each project fell short of your target rate.
This tracker turns every project into an effective hourly rate (fee minus direct costs, divided by actual hours), compares it with your target rate, and shows the hour overrun and the money left on the table against that target. Projects below target are flagged, and the summary gives your overall effective rate, best and worst project, and how many projects fell short.
What's included
- Effective hourly rate for every fixed-fee project
- Hour overrun against your estimate
- Money left on the table against your target rate
- BELOW TARGET flags for underpriced projects
- Overall effective rate, best and worst project, estimate accuracy
- PDF guide with the formulas, a worked example and quoting tips
Who it's for
- Freelance designers, developers and writers
- Consultants working on fixed fees
- Small agencies pricing client projects
- Anyone moving from hourly to project pricing
You get: freelance_project_profitability_tracker.xlsx (Settings, Projects, Summary) and this guide.
Works in Excel 2016 or later, Excel for Mac and Excel on the web; opens in Google Sheets and LibreOffice.
This workbook is a tracking tool, not financial, tax or legal advice. It does not calculate income tax or self-employment tax.

$12. Link in bio.
